issues.description: PR title/description, metadata, and check name disagree about identity and the MANUAL state.
issues.detail: PR title and description say 'multiple network interfaces' with PASS/FAIL semantics, while the directory, files, CheckID, and CHANGELOG say 'single_network_interface' and the code adds an undocumented MANUAL state for GKE. Pick one canonical name and document MANUAL in metadata, or drop the GKE branch. A check with ambiguous identity cannot ship.

issues.description: GKE exemption uses string-prefix on instance.name instead of the real managed-by-GKE signal.
issues.detail: Detecting GKE-managed nodes via `instance.name.startswith('gke-')` is spoofable and unrelated to the property being checked. The API exposes the `goog-gke-node` label and managed-instance-group ancestry — use one of those. Either capture that signal in the Instance model and key off it, or drop the carve-out and document the false-positive in Notes.

issues.description: Zero-interface branch silently returns PASS and has no test coverage.
issues.detail: When `interface_count == 0`, status stays at the default PASS while status_extended says the VM has no NICs — violating the implied 'single NIC' postcondition. The branch is also untested. Either flag it explicitly (FAIL or MANUAL) or remove it, and add a test for the chosen behavior.

`network_interfaces: list[NetworkInterface] = []` uses a shared mutable default. Even if Pydantic copies it today, prefer `Field(default_factory=list)` and match the style already used elsewhere in the model. Low risk, easy fix.

issues.description: Parallel `public_ip` loop should fold into the new NetworkInterface struct.
issues.detail: `public_ip` is still computed by a separate pass over accessConfigs while NetworkInterface only stores name/network/subnetwork. Move accessConfigs/natIP into NetworkInterface and derive `public_ip` as `any(nic.public_ip for nic in instance.network_interfaces)` so there is one pass and one source of truth.

issues.description: `ip_forward` signal mentioned in Notes but never honored.
issues.detail: Metadata Notes call out network virtual appliances as legitimate multi-NIC, and `ip_forward` already exists on the Instance model. Either emit MANUAL when `ip_forward=True` and multi-NIC, or remove the claim from Notes. Don't leave the data on the floor.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on NEEDS-WORK. The check's identity is ambiguous: PR title and description say 'multiple network interfaces' with PASS/FAIL, while the directory, CheckID, CHANGELOG, and an undocumented MANUAL state say otherwise. The GKE exemption uses a spoofable `name.startswith('gke-')` heuristic instead of the available `goog-gke-node` label or MIG ancestry. The zero-interface branch silently PASSes and is untested. Smaller cleanups around Pydantic mutable defaults, an unused `ip_forward` signal, and folding the parallel `public_ip` loop into NetworkInterface round out the list.
